stories.title: 15K-SF Trader Joe’s Store Planned for Joliet Commons Retail Center
stories.excerpt: Marquee Capital, owner of Joliet Commons, and Mid-America Asset Management announced that Trader Joe’s will join the tenant lineup at Joliet Commons. The grocer will occupy approximately 15,000 square feet in the former JoAnn space, adding to the center’s mix of national retailers and everyday conveniences for the surrounding community. Trader Joe’s is expected to open by the end of the year. “Trader Joe’s is the kind of tenant shoppers plan their week around, and backfilling this space with a grocer of its caliber changes how often people come to Joliet Commons,” said Bob DelGhingaro, Chief Operating Officer of Marquee Capital. “It complements a lineup that includes Dick’s Sporting Goods, Ross, Ulta Beauty, PetSmart and Barnes & Noble, and it gives the whole center another reason to be part of a customer’s routine.” Joliet Commons is a 228,000-square-foot retail destination owned and operated by Marquee Capital since 2022. Since then, Dick’s Sporting Goods, PetSmart, Ulta Beauty, Ross, Barnes & Noble and DSW have all extended their leases, and Boot Barn has joined as a new tenant. stories.title: Elevating the Successful ‘Housing Is Health Care’ Model in New York
stories.excerpt: A recently released study confirmed — yet again — what members of the affordable housing community have repeatedly maintained: Housing is indeed health care. An analysis conducted for NYC Health + Hospitals’ Housing for Health initiative and MetroPlusHealth, an affordable health plan, found that in the two years after formerly homeless individuals were permanently housed, they experienced a 40 percent reduction in emergency room visits and a 36 percent reduction in inpatient hospital admissions. At the same time, preventative care visits among these tenants increased, as their housing stability gave them the time to more effectively manage their health. Carlina Rivera. Photo: Courtesy NYSASAF. The result was not just better health outcomes and improved living standards for the 250 formerly unhoused individuals who were placed in housing through this partnership, but also a significant Medicaid savings of $17,000 per person — a total of $3.2 million over two years. Added to a wealth of existing data on the link between housing and improved health — both physical and mental — this latest study underscores the importance of making smart, targeted investments that link services with safe, stable and high-quality housing as we continue to address the city’s affordable housing crisis. New York State Association for Affordable Housing (NYSAFAH) members have long recognized the importance of building developments that expand access to care. Two projects, both completed over the past year, exemplify best practices in this space, and were honored at NYSAFAH’s 2026 Awards for Excellence and Innovation event on Nov. 4. Willow Tree Commons, at 225 East 45th Street in Manhattan, received NYSAFAH’s Innovator of the Year award. It replaced a shelter that Project Renewal had run since 1998 in an outdated building that wasn’t originally designed for that purpose. stories.title: MBA: Commercial Mortgage Originations Post Year-Over-Year Decline in Q3 2026
stories.excerpt: Commercial and multifamily mortgage loan originations were 6% lower in the third quarter of 2026 compared to a year earlier, and decreased 5% from Q2 2026, according to the Mortgage Bankers Association’s (MBA) Quarterly Survey of Commercial/Multifamily Mortgage Bankers Originations. By lending source, the GSEs posted the largest annual decline in volume at 36%, while life company volume was up 12%. Year over year, a fall in originations for retail, office, hotel, and multifamily properties led to an overall decrease in lending volumes. There was a 25% Y-O-Y decrease in the dollar volume of loans for retail properties, a 24% decrease for office properties, a 22% decrease for hotel properties and a 5% decrease for multifamily properties. Industrial properties increased 16% and healthcare property loan originations increased 19% Y-O-Y. “Commercial and multifamily lending slowed in the third quarter, with office, retail, and hotel lending trailing last year’s pace,” said Reggie Booker, MBA’s associate VP of commercial research. “Lending trends varied across capital sources. Life insurance companies continued to increase their lending activity while CMBS volumes declined from the second quarter.” The post MBA: Commercial Mortgage Originations Post Year-Over-Year Decline in Q3 2026 appeared first on Connect CRE.

stories.title: Kids Art Studio ColorPop Workshop to Open at Tribeca’s 450 Washington Street
stories.excerpt: A pop of color can certainly brighten your day. ColorPop Workshop, an art studio offering children ages 3 to 15 a variety of classes, has inked a 1,000-square-foot deal at the base of Related Companies’ 450 Washington Street in Manhattan’s Tribeca neighborhood, according to tenant broker Meridian Retail Leasing. The length of the lease, which was signed Nov. 17, was not disclosed. The asking rent was $180 per square foot. Lindsay Zegans from Ripco Real Estate represented the landlord in the deal, while Meridian’s Max Freudenberger and Noam Aziz represented ColorPop Workshop. “ColorPop Workshop has built a loyal following with families uptown and in Southampton, and Tribeca was the natural next step,” Aziz said in a statement. ColorPop offers painting, clay and comics classes, open studio sessions, holiday camps and birthday parties. This will be the studio’s third Manhattan location alongside its spots at 1289 Madison Avenue and 135 East 63rd Street, both on the Upper East Side. “ColorPop is a perfect fit for Tribeca’s growing community of young families, giving kids a vibrant, creative studio right in their own neighborhood,” Zegans told CO. “We’re thrilled to have helped add them to Related’s retail at 450 Washington Street.” Spanning a full block on the Tribeca waterfront, 450 Washington Street is a 176-unit condominium building completed by Related in 2009. The building features ground-floor retail space and amenities including a private landscaped courtyard and a 12th-floor roof deck. Amanda Schiavo can be reached at aschiavo@commercialobserver.com.

stories.title: Speed Bay Picks Up 10-Building N. Houston Industrial Park
stories.excerpt: Speed Bay Group acquired Greens Road Industrial Park, a 10-building, 249,169-square-foot multi-tenant industrial property in North Houston. Cole Properties was the seller. Greens Road Industrial Park, which will be rebranded as Airway Logistics Park under Speed Bay’s management, is currently 95% leased and offers dock-high and grade-level loading in a predominantly cross-dock configuration. Across 20 suites, the average suite size is approximately 12,500 square feet. The property also includes three fenced and secured outdoor storage yards and 6.9 acres of excess land on the southern edge of the site. The park is immediately adjacent to George Bush Intercontinental Airport (IAH). Jimmy Mulvihill, Vice Chairman of Speed Bay, added: “Shallow bay industrial is an often-overlooked asset class…we see a significant opportunity to build a scaled, vertically integrated platform that provides businesses with the functional space they need.” Speed Bay Warehouse Solutions, the operating platform of Speed Bay Group, will oversee leasing, property management and tenant services at Airway Logistics Park. stories.title: Overland Sheepskin Co. to Open First DC Store on M Street
stories.excerpt: Overland Sheepskin Co., an American heritage brand known for handcrafted sheepskin and leather outerwear and accessories, will open its first Washington, D.C. storefront in Georgetown. Located at 3067 M Street NW, the store will feature the brand’s coats, footwear, accessories and home goods. Overland signed a lease with EastBanc, Inc. and Acadia Realty Trust, co-owners of the Georgetown Portfolio, and plans to open by the end of the year. Overland joins a growing mix of fashion and lifestyle brands along M Street. EastBanc and Acadia Realty Trust continue to add new brands to the portfolio’s retail lineup.“The best retail gives people a reason to walk in, look around and discover something they weren’t expecting,” said Philippe Lanier, CEO of EastBanc. “Overland does that exceptionally well. It has a distinct point of view, with beautifully made products, a strong Western sensibility and a mix that goes far beyond what people might expect from the name.” The post Overland Sheepskin Co. to Open First DC Store on M Street appeared first on Connect CRE.

stories.title: Define Living Starts Work on 388-Unit Houston Apartment Community
stories.excerpt: Define Living is looking to redefine what a wellness-focused apartment community can be. The company’s newest venture, Define: Park Row, will have a dedicated Wellbeing Director who will meet with every resident and guide them on their personal wellbeing journeys. The 388-apartment community sits on 10.4 acres in West Houston’s Energy Corridor and is scheduled to open in Fall 2027. Define: Park Row is located in Wolff Companies’ Central Park master-planned community, off Interstate 10. Seven four-story residential buildings will offer 388 one- and two-bedroom apartments ranging from 657 to 1,089 square feet. Amenities will include a boutique fitness studio for indoor cycling, yoga, trampolines and DEFINE fitness classes, along with an infrared sauna, a cold plunge, a cooking demonstration area and space for residents to gather. Outdoors, residents will have a pool, two pickleball courts, a dog park and nearby trails. Mucasey & Associates is the architect, and Blazer Building is the general contractor. stories.title: CRE Positioned to Withstand 2022 Repeat Amid Rising Rates: NYU Schack Panelists
stories.excerpt: While the commercial real estate industry may be contending with multiple interest rate hikes in 2027, the industry is better equipped today to avoid market dislocation that occurred in 2022, according to debt investors at the 59th annual New York University Schack Institute of Real Estate Capital Markets conference. Unlike 2022, when financing sources were limited, CRE owners now have far more options to access capital through banks, insurance companies and private lenders, said Michael Wiebolt, global chief investment officer of Blackstone Real Estate Debt Strategies. The Federal Reserve began aggressively hiking interest rates starting in March 2022, resulting in valuation dips across a number of CRE properties and owners unable to gain new financing amid higher borrowing costs. “We went through a protracted period beginning in 2022 of pretty limited availability of debt capital,” said Wiebolt during the NYU conference’s global finance and capital markets panel held Thursday morning at the Pierre Hotel in Midtown Manhattan. “That’s a very different dynamic than we’re experiencing today” Wiebolt noted that another important distinction between 2022 and late 2026 is the oversupply dynamics that were at play then in certain asset classes. He said today construction activity has been down significantly in recent years, which should create a “tailwind for accelerating fundamental performance” that could offset some of the capital value impacts from rising interest rates. Another factor that should position the CRE market for near-term sustained higher borrowing costs is disciplined underwriting from lenders over the past few years, according to Mark Romanczuk, head of Americas CRE finance at Goldman Sachs. stories.title: Aerospace and Defense Overtake Tech as L.A.’s Biggest VC Magnet
stories.excerpt: Aerospace and defense have overtaken the traditional tech sector as the top recipients of major venture capital investments in Greater Los Angeles, further fueling demand for industrial and advanced manufacturing space across Southern California. Companies in the overlapping industries have attracted $20.6 billion in funding since 2020, more than double the $10 billion raised by technology companies over the same period, according to a new JLL report on funding rounds of at least $500 million in the L.A., Long Beach and Anaheim metro areas. The shift has accelerated in 2026. Aerospace and defense companies accounted for 72 percent of all major venture funding tracked by JLL so far this year. By comparison, in 2021, tech companies took 74 percent of VC funding. Major venture funding overall has increased 547 percent since its 2023 low, while late-stage rounds accounted for 46 percent of the capital raised. Companies receiving investments through rounds of at least $500 million collectively signed more than 4.8 million square feet of office and industrial leases across the region since 2020. The influx of capital is helping to prop up some of L.A. County’s industrial submarkets even as traditional warehouse demand slows. Aerospace and defense tenants signed more than 400,000 square feet of new leases in the South Bay during the third quarter, keeping Class A industrial vacancy at 4.6 percent, according to JLL. Overall South Bay industrial vacancy stood at 5.3 percent in the third quarter, down from 7.4 percent a year earlier. In the Mid-Cities — the municipalities near the border with Orange County — vacancy declined to 6.3 percent from 7.2 percent annually, while Central L.A. recorded 4.5 percent vacancy, down from 7.1 percent, per JLL data. The momentum contrasts with the broader market, where industrial leasing volume fell approximately 30 percent from the second quarter. stories.title: South Florida Casino to Rebrand as Margaritaville
stories.excerpt: Fontainebleau Development and Margaritaville on Thursday unveiled plans for a $300 million redevelopment of the Big Easy Casino in Hallandale Beach, Fla., as Margaritaville Casino, set to open in the first half of 2028. The casino last month told the Hallandale Beach Planning and Zoning Board of its plans to develop a new 214,428-square-foot casino with a parking garage at 831 North Federal Highway. The new casino will feature a gaming floor with slot machines and a poker room, plus restaurants, bars and live entertainment, Fontainebleau Development said in a statement. Margaritaville Casino will have “a dedicated sports concept,” the developer said, although the Seminole Tribe of Florida holds exclusive rights to sports gambling in Florida. The project is expected to create 400 permanent jobs. The 24-acre site is home to a repurposed greyhound track that opened in the 1930s. The facility added slot machines in 2004 and opened as the Big Easy Casino in 2018. Jeffrey Soffer, chairman and CEO of Fontainebleau Development, acquired the property in 2018. Despite the involvement of Soffer – who operates the Fontainebleau Las Vegas – the Big Easy ranks dead last in slot machine revenue among South Florida’s eight state-sanctioned casinos. The Big Easy’s slots brought in $38 million in revenue in the 2025-26 fiscal year, a fraction of Magic City’s $148 million, according to the Florida Gaming Commission.
